subject: Get a life!
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Alex Vindman for Florida
body:
This is cutting into nap time.
# [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1135?t=1&akid=860%2E3892029%2Ej7rRN-)

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/av-em-q32026?refcode=em260709-1&refcode2=860_3892029_j7rRN-&akid=860%2E3892029%2Ej7rRN-)
---
Hey Peter! This is Larry David. Surprised to hear from me? Well, I’m as surprised as you are. You think I wanted to do this? This is cutting into nap time. But I couldn’t say no to Alex Vindman. He’s running for Senate in Florida. I like that Vindman. The man is everything I’m not, which should give you some idea of what a tremendous person he is.
The guy’s a hero — a real one. He sacrificed his career to testify in front of Congress about how Trump tried to blackmail Zelensky, the President of Ukraine.
You know, I’m a nice guy. I don’t like to criticize people, but I’m willing to bet that the woman running against him wouldn’t sacrifice her career for anything. I’m also willing to bet that every vote she’ll ever cast will be because Trump wanted her to vote that way:
“Yes, Mr. President! Whatever you say, Mr. President. You’re the greatest, Mr. President. Build more monuments to yourself, Mr. President? I’ll vote for it! Gut the Affordable Care Act? I’ll vote for it! Go to war with Iran without a plan to end it? I’ll support it. Use your office to enrich yourself and your family? I won’t say a word. Do anything I can to help you distract from the Epstein files? Sure, here's some more UFO footage! Lie every second of every day? I’ll go along with it, because I’m a puppet and I don’t have a mind of my own. I’m just a little sock.”
Vindman is not a puppet. He has a moral compass that doesn’t allow him to sell out. His family immigrated from Ukraine. They had nothing. He loves this country. He loves it so much it’s almost off-putting. I love it too, but come on. Get a life, Vindman! There’s more to life than serving America.
**Now here’s the awful part...Right, you got it. Money. Alas, you can’t get elected without money for a campaign.** I get it if you don’t want to give anything. Who wants to give money to someone you don’t know? Who wants to give money to someone you know?!
[**But even if it’s a small amount, it might be worth it if you elect someone who’s different, who has a backbone, and who’s actually a good guy. And who knows — you might personally need something from your senator one day. And this I guarantee — he will respond. And if he can help you, he will. As my mother used to say, “He’s a living doll.”**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/av-em-q32026?refcode=em260709-1&amount=3&refcode2=860_3892029_j7rRN-&akid=860%2E3892029%2Ej7rRN-)

body:
What y’all tell me matters.

| [](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.)
---
Peter,
It’s Tim Burchett.
Now look, I know politicians send about 147 emails a day. Most of ’em sound like they were written by some 24-year-old consultant wearing loafers with no socks in a DC coffee shop.
This ain’t that.
I’ve been talking to folks all across this country, and let me tell ya something: Americans are fed up.

body:
| 🇺🇸 Today, we celebrate 250 years — and ask for your help _You’re getting this message from[ _Power the Polls_](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4508?t=1&akid=9050%2E934366%2EnSFU6x) because you signed up to learn about serving as a poll worker. If you no longer wish to hear from us, [_please unsubscribe here_](https://act.powerthepolls.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=9050.934366.nSFU6x&t=2&akid=9050%2E934366%2EnSFU6x). Marking emails as spam can affect our ability to reach others with important information. _
# [](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/42?t=3&akid=9050%2E934366%2EnSFU6x)
Hey Peter— Over the weekend we commemorated America’s 250th birthday, it’s a historic milestone in the bold experiment we call democracy. The fabric of the United States is tied together by all its citizens stepping up and doing our part: from jury duty to voting, we all keep our government running. Every state will hold elections this fall, millions will cast their ballots, and in order for that to be accessible and efficient we need thousands of poll workers to keep precincts running smoothly. [**Power the Polls can think of no better way to celebrate this anniversary than by recruiting 250 poll workers in each state. Sign up to become a poll worker and protect the next 250 years.**](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4922?t=4&akid=9050%2E934366%2EnSFU6x) [](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4922?t=5&akid=9050%2E934366%2EnSFU6x) Our democracy works when we all show up.**You’re already stepping up, can you pass this invite along to your loved ones who you’d like to work the polls with?** It’s rewarding, engaging, and most states pay you for your time and service. Get started on your application today and help fulfill the promise of democracy: [Start Your Application](https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4888?t=6&akid=9050%2E934366%2EnSFU6x) Thanks, —Power the Polls Team
---

This email was sent to [dpwillis67@gmail.com](mailto:dpwillis67@gmail.com). You received this message because you are subscribed to Power the Polls' mailing list. [Click here to unsubscribe.](https://act.powerthepolls.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?ak_proof=1&akid=9050.934366.nSFU6x&t=7&akid=9050%2E934366%2EnSFU6x) If you have any questions, please contact us at [info@powerthepolls.org](mailto:info@powerthepolls.org) and a member of our team will be in touch.

name: Dr. Vanessa Enoch
subject: America Needs New Leadership—And Ohio Can't Afford More of the Same
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Enoch, Catherine Johnson, Treasurer
body:
The ongoing war in Iran is not happening in isolation. Every day it's affecting Americans here at home. It influences federal spending...

| | | | | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | Hello Peter,
Washington is hoping Americans will stay quiet.Stay quiet while families struggle to pay their bills.Stay quiet while our tax dollars flow overseas.Stay quiet while utility costs continue to rise.Stay quiet while powerful interests reshape our communities without meaningful public input.
I don't believe that's what democracy looks like.
The ongoing war in Iran and around the world are not happening in isolation. Every day they affect Americans here at home. They influence federal spending priorities, contribute to economic uncertainty, strain supply chains, and leave many families wondering why it feels harder each month to get ahead.
Meanwhile, right here in Ohio, we're facing another challenge that deserves far more public discussion.
Massive data centers are being built across our state. These facilities place enormous demands on our electric grid, water resources, and infrastructure. Ohio families are paying the price when electricity demand rises, communities change, and billions of dollars in tax incentives are awarded to some of the world's largest corporations.
These are not partisan issues.They are kitchen-table issues.Parents wonder why groceries cost more.Seniors worry about rising utility bills.Small businesses struggle with increasing operating costs.Working families are doing everything right—and still falling behind.
Washington has had plenty of opportunities to put working people first. Too often, career politicians have chosen politics over people.
I refuse to accept that this is the best we can do.
I'm running for Congress because our district deserves leadership that asks hard questions, demands accountability, and puts Ohio families ahead of special interests.We need leaders who will fight for affordable energy, responsible economic development, fiscal responsibility, strong infrastructure, good-paying jobs, and policies that strengthen our communities—not simply enrich the most powerful corporations.
But I can't do this alone.
Unlike career politicians backed by Washington insiders, this campaign is powered by people like you.
Will you make a contribution today of [$10, $25, $50, $100](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=eabd1afae8&e=c6e7dff14c), or whatever you can afford to help us build a campaign that puts the people of Ohio's 8th Congressional District first?
Every dollar helps us reach more voters, print campaign literature, recruit volunteers, place yard signs, and build the grassroots movement we need to win.
This election is about more than one congressional seat.
It's about deciding whether we'll continue accepting the status quo—or whether we'll choose courageous new leadership that will speak up when others remain silent.If you're ready for new leadership in Washington, I'm asking you to stand with me today.
Together, we can build a government that works for working families again.
With gratitude,
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**
Democratic Nominee for Congress
Ohio's 8th Congressional District
P.S. History doesn't change because people stay silent. It changes because ordinary citizens decide to get involved. Please donate and volunteer today and help us bring new leadership to Washington.
Paid for by the Committee to Elect Enoch, Catherine Johnson, Treasurer.

You may know me as the author of _Too Much and Never Enough,_ or as someone who has spent years sounding the alarm about my uncle, Donald. [**_I launched Transcend PAC to fund the candidates fighting Donald's corruption every day, who will strengthen the democracy my uncle is trying to destroy. If you can give, please split a donation between Transcend PAC and Blue Amp Action, and then read on to learn why I believe this moment calls for something transformational._**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13928?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.09_Mary-Trump-Uncle_B1_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=5&akid=2622%2E259176%2EidVZfY) | [BECOME A FOUNDING DONOR TODAY >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13928?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.09_Mary-Trump-Uncle_B1_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=6&akid=2622%2E259176%2EidVZfY)
---
**Here's what I need you to understand about my uncle: Donald is a weak man.**
That might seem like an odd thing to say about somebody who holds such a powerful position, but that's exactly the danger. Every day, as Donald deteriorates – psychologically, emotionally, and cognitively – he grows more desperate, increasing the risk to the rest of us.
Strong people do not rig the system in their favor. They don't silence critics. They don't seek to control the institutions designed to hold them accountable. **Donald does all of those things — because he has to, and he knows it. His behavior isn't evidence of strength – it's evidence of its absence.**
The comprehensiveness with which Donald and the complicit Republican Party are attempting to dismantle our institutions and take away our rights, in service to maintaining their hold on power and self-enrichment, should also make clear what is at stake.
Under Donald’s so-called leadership, the Republicans in Congress have stood by while our nation’s alliances have become strained; illegal wars have been started; and our institutions have been weakened and, in some cases, dismantled entirely.
I believe we are going to prevail. But when corrupt leaders like Donald and the sycophantic enablers in his inner circle go unchecked or unchallenged, they can do enormous damage. The antidote is to assemble a coalition of people who refuse to look away and are willing to take action.
**That’s why I launched Transcend PAC. Together, we’ll fund candidates who believe in public service and who will work to fulfill the promise of American democracy.** Because we deserve representatives who understand what’s at stake and are prepared to meet the moment.
[**_If you're able, please split a donation between Transcend PAC and Blue Amp Action today. Your contribution funds the organizing and the advocacy that will ensure no voice is silenced and all of our voices are heard. Every dollar will go toward undoing the damage my uncle and the Republican Party have done so we, together, can build something better._**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13928?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.09_Mary-Trump-Uncle_B1_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=7&akid=2622%2E259176%2EidVZfY)

The Department of Justice just sent letters to election officials in all 50 states with a chilling threat--If a non-citizen votes, you will be personally prosecuted.
The letter also insists that state officials respond within five days to inform the justice department how it will ensure compliance "with federal laws." To avoid potential criminal charges, the DOJ "encourages" officials to contact them to "discuss steps your state should take to maintain clean voter lists as required by law."
If you've been following our work, you know that we've been sounding the alarm about the Trump admin's attempt to seize voter data. Voter data that includes sensitive information such as name, address, and party registration.
The Trump admin has been using this voter data to purge voter rolls using the "SAVE" database. A database a judge ruled was illegal because of major violations of Americans' privacy rights. And one that has been proven in court to wrongfully purge Democrats from voter rolls.
This letter isn't subtle. It's a blatant attempt to intimidate election officials into turning over your sensitive voter data.

# **US strikes 90 Iranian targets overnight as Gulf states face missile attacks**
The US military **[struck roughly 90 targets inside Iran Wednesday,](https://substack.com/redirect/d11b59a1-7adb-41aa-b168-9f3e2ca5f463?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** dramatically escalating the conflict after President Donald Trump declared the ceasefire effectively over. CENTCOM said the strikes targeted Iranian military infrastructure tied to missile, drone, and maritime threats following Tehran's continued attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran responded by warning of "grave consequences" for US allies involved in the operation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d11b59a1-7adb-41aa-b168-9f3e2ca5f463?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Kuwait intercepted three ballistic missiles, one cruise missile, and ten hostile drones in its airspace** Thursday morning, with debris from the interceptions causing material damage across multiple locations and injuring one person. Kuwaiti armed forces remain on heightened alert.

"A right to attend that does not include the ability to perceive what is happening is not meaningful presence at all," the filing states, warning that withholding evidence from public view breeds speculation and erodes public trust in the judicial system. Robinson, 23, faces aggravated murder charges carrying a potential death penalty for the September 2025 assassination of Kirk outside a Utah Valley University event. # Iran and Ceasefire
* **U.S. continues to bomb Iran:** U.S. Central Command[ announced](https://substack.com/redirect/f7a48a01-ba68-428a-a992-fc84478a9f42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday that it was conducting additional strikes on Iran.
* According to CENTCOM, the strikes targeted sites intended to "further degrade" Iran's ability to threaten shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. On Thursday morning, it reported that 90 strikes were carried out overnight.
* The U.S. struck facilities at Iranshahr airport in the southeastern Sistan and Baluchistan province, damaging the airport's flight operations building and meteorological station and killing a firefighter, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.
* U.S. strikes killed three people in Ahvaz, and shrapnel from an attack damaged a hospital in Chahbahar.
* The U.S. also [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/bc98dc3c-e04f-45a5-8191-4713dcadcd5a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Bushehr province on Thursday, though the region's governor insisted that the strikes did not hit the area's nuclear power plant, according to Al Jazeera.
* Wednesday's strikes follow strikes reported in Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Sirik, Bushehr, Chabahar and Konarak on Tuesday. Attacks on Tuesday and Wednesday killed 14 and brought about 78 total hospitalizations, Iran's Health Ministry reported on Thursday, with 47 of these cases requiring continued hospitalization.
* Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the newest wave of U.S. attacks on the country on Thursday, calling Washington's justification--that it attacked in response to Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz--a "false pretext".

* **Iran launches retaliatory attacks:**
* Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) [said](https://substack.com/redirect/f6d9bd7c-4362-4626-ab36-bf9b865d46a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) early Thursday that it launched a joint missile and drone operation targeting U.S. bases at Arifjan and Ali Al Salem in Kuwait, and Juffair and Sheikh Isa in Bahrain, adding that "the aggressions of the child-killing U.S. army" would not go unanswered, according to the Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA).
* In response to these attacks, sirens were set off in Bahrain and Kuwait's defense ministry sent residents several alerts.
* A spokesperson for Kuwait's defense ministry [confirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/368be8a5-96c3-4f1f-9178-c96a488295e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday that one person was wounded during attacks by Iran across the country. The ministry reported the victim was hospitalized and in stable condition after being struck by falling debris, but did not specify where the incident occurred.
* Jordan's armed forces also [said](https://substack.com/redirect/9281b9c9-90e0-4107-9139-6557d306bb9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its air defence systems intercepted eight missiles "launched from Iran toward Jordanian territory" on Thursday, Jordanian outlet Al-Mamlaka, reported. A military spokesperson said debris from the interceptions fell in several areas but caused no casualties or material damage.
* **U.S. potentially preparing to strike Iran for weeks, Axios reports:** The White House is [preparing](https://substack.com/redirect/74356ac6-75db-4f16-b50d-f9bb8087167b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for what could become a multi-day or even multi-week military campaign against Iran centered on the Strait of Hormuz, Axios, a frequent source of U.S. and Israeli leaks throughout the war, reported on Wednesday.
* One U.S. official reportedly threatened to "slap" Iran "a bit," "so they understand we're not fucking around." The same official said the duration of the strikes will depend on Tehran's response.
* Trump told reporters on Air Force One that Iran's representative had "called a little while ago" and that they "want to make a deal"--a claim he made without providing evidence. Iran did not confirm any direct outreach.
* U.S. officials also told Axios that "reopening" the Strait of Hormuz and "restoring freedom of navigation" have become the administration's primary military objectives, as Iran has insisted the waterway will only operate on its terms.
* Vice President JD Vance told reporters on Wednesday that U.S. strikes "are just going to keep on happening until they open up that lane and stop shooting at ships."
* Regarding the Strait, Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's lead negotiator and parliament speaker, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e82c3d99-990c-4397-b27c-024e98edf7a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a post on X it would "only open with 'Iranian arrangements,' not American threats." He also warned Washington that it "still [hadn't] learned that bullying and breaking promises are no longer cost-free." "Let me put it plainly, he said, "if you strike, you'll get hit."
* Traffic through the Strait [slowed](https://substack.com/redirect/782a4d54-7672-4662-909c-b878c7a034fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to a near standstill on Thursday, Bloomberg reported. Ship-tracking data showed most vessel movements were confined to the Iran-approved route along the waterway's northern side, while the U.S.-backed Omani shipping corridor saw little activity. Among larger vessels, only a U.S.-sanctioned supertanker departing the Persian Gulf and an Iranian-flagged container ship were visible, although some ships may have been transiting with their tracking systems switched off, the outlet noted.
* **Iran says Khamenei funeral proceeding despite U.S. attacks** : Iranian officials [said](https://substack.com/redirect/440ffa23-05da-4b26-9cf2-4a875b249bc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday that recent U.S. attacks have not disrupted the funeral procession for the slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, whose body was flown to Mashhad to be buried after week-long processions in Tehran, Qom, and the Iraqi cities of Karbala and Najaf, Al Jazeera reported.
* Officials said an overnight strike that knocked out the railway linking Tehran to Mashhad had not altered plans, and attributed an eight-hour postponement of the burial, originally set for 6 a.m. local time near the shrine of Imam Reza, to heavy crowds in Iraq rather than the attacks.
* In a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/42048743-699c-4adc-934a-a54622dec901?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) issued on Thursday, Iran's Foreign Ministry accused the U.S. of targeting the railway route to Mashhad in an attempt to overshadow the funeral ceremonies of Khamenei, adding the attack reflected its "inability to comprehend the glory of Iranian patriotism" after the Iranian public's "magnificent and unparalleled" turnout at the funeral, IRNA reported.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli forces demolish homes in Hadatha, bomb Houla in south Lebanon:** Israeli forces [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/f528581b-ae92-4be0-9ed3-57545d1ac90b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a demolition operation targeting several houses in the town of Hadatha in the Bint Jbeil district, the National News Agency (NNA) reported Thursday, despite a U.S.-backed "ceasefire" signed with Lebanon.
* Israeli forces also bombed the town of Houla in the Marjayoun district, according to NNA. The Israeli army also carried out a series of demolitions overnight and at dawn in the towns of Khiam and Taybeh in Marjayoun.
* **Trump says Israel will withdraw from southern Lebanon; Israel 's defense minister says it won't: **U.S. President Donald Trump [told](https://substack.com/redirect/cabebfc8-3994-412c-a15e-369fb1133e9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reporters on Wednesday that he thought Israel would withdraw from southern Lebanon.
* "I think they want to," he said to reporters, despite recent statements from Netanyahu to the contrary, and citing the recent "framework" deal as the reason for the withdrawal. "Yeah, they'll leave. And I think it's going to work out very well," Trump said.
* Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz rejected these claims on Thursday, saying Israel would stay in Lebanon as long as it deemed necessary, and that it "did not ask permission to enter Lebanon" and "does not need permission to stay in Lebanon."
* **Hezbollah: Lebanon-Israel framework "serves Israel entirely": **Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem [said](https://substack.com/redirect/b39c1831-1a88-4672-bc10-18323c760579?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday the Lebanon-Israel framework agreement "serves Israel entirely" and called for it to be scrapped, arguing it was unconstitutional, NNA reported. Speaking during a public gathering, Qassem said Israel had committed "hundreds" of ceasefire violations and urged Lebanese authorities to pursue only indirect negotiations. He also said there could be "no solution except Israeli withdrawal" in exchange for the deployment of the Lebanese army south of the Litani River, alongside an end to Israeli attacks, the release of detainees, reconstruction, and the return of displaced residents. He reaffirmed Hezbollah's support for the U.S.-Iran MOU, saying the group would remain committed to resistance.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded:** Over the last 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed, one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks, and 17 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,118 killed, with 173,615 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,092 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,507, while 799 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Israeli attacks on Gaza continue on Thursday:**
* An Israeli drone strike [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/5104e59f-1712-4fd3-ad28-645b491b5627?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two Palestinians and wounded several others west of Khan Younis, southern Gaza on Thursday, WAFA reported. Another Palestinian was also killed in a drone strike on a vehicle west of Gaza City.
* **Israeli attacks kill at least eight Palestinians on Wednesday:** Israeli attacks across Gaza on Wednesday killed at least eight Palestinians, including multiple children, including an employee of the World Central Kitchen.
* Israeli forces [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/57d6d075-cbfe-417c-a0bd-86c8922142c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a driver working for a World Central Kitchen partner logistics company, the charity announced on Wednesday, while he was transporting aid from the Kerem Shalom crossing to a WCK warehouse in Gaza.
* An Israeli airstrike on Gaza City's Sheikh Radwan neighborhood killed two, while a strike on a vehicle west of Gaza City on Wednesday evening [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/090ba2eb-eee3-43b8-b821-1d3ddb8ceaea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) one Palestinian and wounded several others, WAFA reported.
* **Israeli court rejects imprisoned physician 's plea: **The**** Israeli government [responded](https://substack.com/redirect/48d78891-5c69-44c1-b3dc-2240ed5152c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday to a High Court petition over the detention of Gaza physician Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, saying he has been examined several times since being transferred to the underground Rakefet detention facility, following reports of severe abuse by Israeli forces.
* The government also asked the court to dismiss, without a hearing, PHRI's petition seeking the release of 14 Gaza doctors, including Dr. Abu Safiya, held without charge.
* Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI) argued that the state failed to explain why the examinations were necessary, what they found, or to respond to allegations from his lawyer that he suffered severe injuries and repeated loss of consciousness. The group said the decision raises additional questions about Dr. Safiya's well-being.
* Also on Wednesday, two more U.S. members of Congress called for Dr. Abu Safiya's release. Sen. Bernie Sanders [charged](https://substack.com/redirect/a344f670-a4b4-47eb-886c-4ea43d1016ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Israel of "kidnapping" Dr. Safiya because he refused to abandon one of Gaza's last hospitals, "even after Israel killed his own son in a drone strike," and unequivocally demanded his "immediate" release.
* Florida Democrat Valerie Foushee joined Sanders--and Sen. Chris Van Hollen and Democratic congressional nominee Darializa Avila Chevalier before her--in calling for Abu Safiya's release, saying she is "deeply disturbed" by his detention and reports of his abuse in prison.

* **Hamas delegation returns to Cairo for negotiations:** A Hamas delegation led by the group's Gaza head, Dr. Khalil al-Hayya, [arrived](https://substack.com/redirect/a9637033-1460-431d-9395-6725d7685481?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Cairo on Wednesday to continue ceasefire negotiations with Egyptian and other mediators, according to a statement from senior official Taher Al-Nunu.
* Al-Nunu said that talks aim to "secure a lasting ceasefire," advance the agreement to its second phase while completing the implementation of its first phase, increase humanitarian aid into Gaza, and accelerate the transfer of governance responsibilities to the National Committee for Administration of Gaza, operating under Trump's "Board of Peace," following the dissolution of the Strip's administration earlier this week.
* **Abbas sets Nov. 28 as date for Palestinian legislative elections:** Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/28454c9e-462a-4066-b9eb-0351e18cd1db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a decree on Thursday setting Saturday, November 28, 2026, as the date for legislative elections, calling on Palestinians in East Jerusalem, the occupied West Bank and the Gaza Strip to participate, according to WAFA.
* Abbas, who has remained in office since 2005 after repeatedly postponing elections, announced what would be the first parliamentary vote since 2006, when Hamas defeated his Fatah movement. In June, he amended the election law, requiring candidates to endorse the Palestine Liberation Organization as the sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people. Hamas rejected the changes, saying they entrenched political monopoly and lacked national consensus.
* **Israel 's "Crimson Thread" barrier cuts off Palestinian farms in Jordan Valley**: Israeli forces are constructing a 22-kilometer separation wall and military road through the Al-Forat farm near Tubas in the northern West Bank, part of a planned 500-kilometer "Crimson Thread" barrier that would seal off the Jordan Valley from the rest of Palestine, Drop Site reports.
* Farmer Muad Abdelreziq told Drop Site that Israel had cut water access to 400 dunams of farmland for five days and destroyed irrigation pipelines, and a January petition by Tubas residents estimating $200 million in annual economic damage led to a court injunction that Israel's military successfully rescinded days after the U.S. and Israel launched their war on Iran on March 3.
* "I cannot irrigate the herbs, I cannot irrigate the melons," one farmer said about the changes. "I cannot replace the water lines. All these families will have nothing. We will have to stop."
* **Read the latest from Drop Site 's Maysa Mustafa [here](https://substack.com/redirect/4cd6c4b6-b846-4bec-ab72-e4cf3c9c671d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and watch Mustafa's video dispatch [here](https://substack.com/redirect/f05ec35c-c665-404a-a44b-e7ac2a6b9426?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**

# U.S. News
_By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at[ Julian@dropsitenews.com](https://substack.com/redirect/7e756d0c-284a-485a-a2ec-40ad0ac136aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
* **Graham Platner drops out of Maine Senate race:** Democratic Senate candidate **Graham Platner** [withdrew](https://substack.com/redirect/51c93cea-8b44-4d3a-995d-7b10993e7c02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the race on Wednesday after a week in which he faced multiple allegations of sexual misconduct, including a rape allegation.
* In a video posted to X, he called the accusations "all false" and told supporters that he was ending his campaign because the "political reality" was that party leaders and major donors "are going to take everything away from us," making it impossible to continue.
* Maine Democrats now have until July 27 to choose a replacement for the November race against incumbent Republican **Sen. Susan Collins**. In his video statement, Platner urged party leaders to make the selection through an "open, transparent and democratic" process that reflects "the will and the values of the people of Maine," not decisions made "in back rooms."
* The Maine Democratic State Committee voted Wednesday to select a replacement nominee for Graham Platner in the U.S. Senate race through a 600-person nominating convention rather than a statewide caucus, with 500 delegates apportioned by county and the remaining 100 drawn from state committee members. The decision, reported by **David Dayen** at The American Prospect, reverses earlier sourcing that had pointed toward a caucus and threatens to alienate Platner's supporters, who had pushed for an open process. Read TAP's full report on the nominating process [here](https://substack.com/redirect/644b1275-fb01-4023-827b-76cb9ea101ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Also on Wednesday, **Spencer Toth** , who helped design Platner's grassroots campaign strategy and later became the organizing director for the state's Democratic Party, [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/396b0e49-30c2-4fab-83f9-7ea1db8dd777?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his immediate resignation, alleging that the Party was excluding grassroots organizers from the selection of the next nominee and saying he could no longer serve it when its decisions were not "consistent with [his] values." His resignation cited a Tuesday statement from the Party that said that Platner's apparatus would "have no role in determining our next nominee for U.S. Senate, nor in determining what this process would look like."
* **Joint Chiefs ' top legal counsel to step down early amid wave of Pentagon exits: **Brig. Gen. **Eric Widmar** , senior legal counsel to Joint Chiefs of Staff Chair Gen. **Dan Caine** , is [retiring](https://substack.com/redirect/fff718a3-ec77-41e7-8b96-b2f9d4dcf597?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nearly a year ahead of schedule, telling ProPublica he is leaving for personal reasons after two years living apart from his wife.
* Widmar becomes the latest in a string of top military officials to depart the Pentagon since the start of the second Trump administration, following Gen. **Chris Donahue 's** exit last week, Army Chief of Staff Gen. **Randy George 's** ouster in April, and Adm. **Alvin Holsey 's** removal from Southern Command late last year, all reportedly pushed by War Secretary **Pete Hegseth**.
* **Johnson weighs introducing bill to end birthright citizenship:** Speaker of the House **Mike Johnson** is [considering](https://substack.com/redirect/00a9cfb9-e31d-413f-90bd-e8e41026eda6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) bringing legislation to the floor that would bar pregnant women from entering the United States to secure citizenship for their children, according to a report from Politico.
* The largely symbolic measure, unlikely to survive a Senate filibuster, would give Johnson a way to respond to hard-line Republicans pressing for action after the Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's effort to curtail birthright citizenship.
* **Former Wisconsin judge fined $5,000, avoids prison for helping immigrant evade ICE arrest** : Former Milwaukee County Judge**Hannah Dugan** was [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/5930ecf3-70b3-4033-8ac3-dfd404c4bfaa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday to a $5,000 fine rather than prison time by U.S. District Judge**Lynn Adelman** , after being convicted in December of felony obstruction for leading Mexican defendant **Eduardo Flores-Ruiz** through a private jury door in April 2025 as ICE agents sought to arrest him at her Milwaukee County courthouse. Agents ultimately caught and arrested Flores-Ruiz outside after a foot chase, and he was deported in November.

# Other International News
* **U.S. to remove Syria from list of "state sponsors of terror": **The U.S. [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/ab5bccae-071e-4faf-a0f1-11dcecd549fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday that it would delist Syria as a "state sponsor of terror," with Secretary of State Marco Rubio calling the move a "historic step" which would "give the Syrian people a chance at greatness."
* Rubio added that the decision was made because Syria had made "formal assurances" to the U.S. that it would "not support acts of international terrorism in the future."
* The announcement came as Trump met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Ankara on Wednesday. Trump praised al-Sharaa for the "unbelievable job" he had done in Syria. "What a job he's doing," he added.
* The designation has significantly impacted the country's economy since it was announced in 1979. It has limited investment within Syria by preventing U.S.-affiliated companies from doing business in the country and by preventing Syrian companies from banking with U.S.-based financial institutions.
* The U.S. had lifted other sanctions on the country in May, but this delisting is viewed by many as the most significant step the U.S. has taken to benefit al-Sharaa's government.
* **DRC reports 600 Ebola deaths:** At least 600 people have [died](https://substack.com/redirect/191408fd-99fb-434b-8d4d-dac694150b91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, according to data released by the country's government on Wednesday.
* As the outbreak has grown more severe, many healthcare workers in the Ituri province, one of the hardest-hit, have gone on an unofficial strike because they have not been paid, according to the Associated Press. Some workers report not having been paid wages or bonuses since the outbreak was declared on May 15.
* Clinical trials for treatment of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus--the dominant strain in this latest outbreak--have also begun this week, according to Al Jazeera.
* **U.S. migrants arrive in Eswatini:** Eleven more migrants [arrived](https://substack.com/redirect/c4631b29-5410-4cdf-bc81-5abad9ac66f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Eswatini on Wednesday as part of the Trump administration's "third-country" deportation policy.
* Wednesday's arrivals bring the total number of deportees to 29, following the country's receipt of $5.1 million from Washington. Only two of these people have been released and repatriated.
* The "third-country" deportation policy has been challenged as illegal, with lawyers for deportees noting that their clients are being detained after having served time for crimes in the United States.
* **Sudanese Army takes control of Kurmuk:** The Sudanese Army [recaptured](https://substack.com/redirect/ef833aa1-d58b-40fe-ba74-31374b15e70a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the border town of Kurmuk in the Blue Nile region on Wednesday, Sudan Tribune reported, after battles between its forces and those of the Rapid Support Forces and its allied Sudan People's Liberation Movement (SPLM-N).
* The Sudanese Army has set its sights on Kurmuk for several weeks, launching several operations to secure the surrounding area. The town has frequently changed hands during Sudan's civil war, which began in 2023.
* Kurmuk is near Sudan's border with Ethiopia, which the Sudanese government has accused of supporting the RSF by allowing its drones to launch from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport. Ethiopia's government has rejected these allegations.
* Separately, a UN probe found on Wednesday that the RSF's actions in its 2025 siege of El-Fasher, which included mass killings, abductions of women and girls, mass gang rapes and forced starvation, amount to genocide.
* The decision comes after survivors testified to UN human rights officials about being raped in the same room where bodies of recently killed civilians, some of whom were their family members, were still lying on the ground.
* UN officials recently warned about similar conditions in the city of El-Obeid, a city which has been under assault by the RSF's drones, calling the "signs" of human rights abuses "clear and unmistakable."
* **Brazilian police search former president 's home for weapons: **Brazil's federal police [searched](https://substack.com/redirect/2d6640cd-bb0d-4603-86bd-f79220efb62b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the home of former President Jair Bolsonaro for weapons on Wednesday, according to a court ruling reported on by Reuters. Bolsonaro's lawyers insist that nothing was found.
* Last month, a gun registered to Bolsonaro was seized from one of his security guards at a police checkpoint, even though he was required by a court order to surrender all of his weapons.
* Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27-year prison term under house arrest after attempting a coup when he lost the 2022 election to current president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
* Bolsonaro's son, Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro, is Lula's principal right-wing opponent in this year's presidential elections.
* **Trump says he will allow Ukraine to make Patriot interceptors:** At a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Ankara Wednesday, President Donald Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/14a91600-25d0-4a11-b793-724860549a9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he would give Ukraine "a license" to make Patriot missile interceptors, calling the move "pretty cool" and "defensive" and saying it would prevent the Ukrainians from "complaining" about insufficient supply.
* Trump gave no specifics about the license, answering a question about a timeline with only the qualification that "some" could be sent immediately, and that Ukraine would "quickly" be able to produce interceptors of its own.
* He also hinted that the U.S. would be willing to use its "great power" over the companies that produce the interceptors to secure them for Ukraine. Lockheed Martin is the primary manufacturer of this technology
* Trump struck a noticeably warm tone with Zelenskyy, with whom he has clashed in the past. He also said he intended to speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin later in the day, though he provided no further details.
* **Russia bans diesel exports:** Russia [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/d7ac3e45-d549-4fe6-a2e6-a45e7c549ec9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday that it would ban the export of its diesel products until the end of July in an attempt to protect its energy markets from the effects of the war in Ukraine, and following several Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.
* The move, which will significantly tighten the global supply of and demand for refined petroleum products, is expected to have a particular effect on Europe's diesel markets, pushing up costs immediately for farmers and truckers, and eventually for consumers.
* **Ukrainian drones hit Russian tankers:** Ukrainian drones hit a dozen Russian tankers in the Sea of Azov overnight, Ukraine's military [said](https://substack.com/redirect/2e646f29-9b9b-4211-a07d-549f165ee236?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a statement, as Kyiv ramps up a campaign aimed at hitting energy infrastructure and disrupting fuel supplies to Russian forces while isolating Moscow-occupied Crimea.
* **Ireland moves to ban imports from Israeli settlements:** Ireland's Dail [passed](https://substack.com/redirect/06981827-6d35-4eb4-ba7b-08cb09bb6467?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Occupied Territories Bill on Tuesday without a vote, setting Ireland up to become the first European Union country to legislate a ban on imports from Israeli settlements, according to Irish broadcaster RTÉ.
* The bill heads to the Seanad next week and is expected to be law before mid-July, making settlement imports an offense under Ireland's Customs Act, the Irish Times reports.
* The government's version of the bill bans only goods, however, while exempting services, which make up about 70 percent of Ireland's trade with Israel, said a foreign affairs spokesperson for Ireland's Labour Party.
* Taoiseach Micheal Martin has cited legal risk and potential damage to U.S. multinationals in Ireland if the bill is passed, and the Irish Times reported that Ireland's embassy in Washington has also been warned of "consequences" by its American host.
* **Flooding from Tropical Storm Maysak kills 39 in southern China** : Flooding from Tropical Storm Maysak has [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/672e21b5-6e87-44ca-92f5-055a24643383?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 39 people in China's southern Guangxi region, including 26 after a dam breach inundated parts of Nanning, officials said Thursday. About 130,000 people have been evacuated, with more than 8,000 rescuers and 5,700 boats deployed after days of heavy rainfall brought up to 90 cm of rain in the hardest-hit areas. Authorities said floodwaters are receding, but more rain is expected, while work continues to clear debris, disinfect towns, repair roads and restore power.
* **Calls to lift Venezuela sanctions grow amid post-earthquake recovery efforts:** Venezuelan Acting President Delcy Rodriguez [appealed](https://substack.com/redirect/cbf44b5a-d20b-4630-96eb-dac3a8512842?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the U.K. to release 30 tons of gold held by the Bank of England, arguing these resources are vital for reconstruction. Separaely, a coalition of over 100 prominent economists, including Jeffrey Sachs and Isabella Weber, [called on](https://substack.com/redirect/e65e2f63-40c1-4a7d-b463-791cc6648f3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the U.S. to lift all broad economic sanctions, saying the "indiscriminate" measures severely obstruct the humanitarian response and essential post-disaster recovery efforts.

The U.S. also the Bushehr province on Thursday, though the region's governor insisted that the strikes did not hit the area's nuclear power plant, according to Al Jazeera. Wednesday's strikes follow strikes reported in Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Sirik, Bushehr, Chabahar and Konarak on Tuesday. Attacks on Tuesday and Wednesday killed 14 and brought about 78 total hospitalizations, Iran's Health Ministry reported on Thursday, with 47 of these cases requiring continued hospitalization. Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the newest wave of U.S. attacks on the country on Thursday, calling Washington's justification--that it attacked in response to Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz--a "false pretext". Iran launches retaliatory attacks: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) early Thursday that it launched a joint missile and drone operation targeting U.S. bases at Arifjan and Ali Al Salem in Kuwait, and Juffair and Sheikh Isa in Bahrain, adding that "the aggressions of the child-killing U.S. army" would not go unanswered, according to the Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA). In response to these attacks, sirens were set off in Bahrain and Kuwait's defense ministry sent residents several alerts. A spokesperson for Kuwait's defense ministry Thursday that one person was wounded during attacks by Iran across the country. The ministry reported the victim was hospitalized and in stable condition after being struck by falling debris, but did not specify where the incident occurred. Jordan's armed forces also its air defence systems intercepted eight missiles "launched from Iran toward Jordanian territory" on Thursday, Jordanian outlet Al-Mamlaka, reported. A military spokesperson said debris from the interceptions fell in several areas but caused no casualties or material damage. U.S. potentially preparing to strike Iran for weeks, Axios reports: The White House is for what could become a multi-day or even multi-week military campaign against Iran centered on the Strait of Hormuz, Axios, a frequent source of U.S. and Israeli leaks throughout the war, reported on Wednesday. One U.S. official reportedly threatened to "slap" Iran "a bit," "so they understand we're not fucking around." The same official said the duration of the strikes will depend on Tehran's response. Trump told reporters on Air Force One that Iran's representative had "called a little while ago" and that they "want to make a deal"--a claim he made without providing evidence. Iran did not confirm any direct outreach. U.S. officials also told Axios that "reopening" the Strait of Hormuz and "restoring freedom of navigation" have become the administration's primary military objectives, as Iran has insisted the waterway will only operate on its terms. Vice President JD Vance told reporters on Wednesday that U.S. strikes "are just going to keep on happening until they open up that lane and stop shooting at ships." Regarding the Strait, Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's lead negotiator and parliament speaker, in a post on X it would "only open with 'Iranian arrangements,' not American threats." He also warned Washington that it "still [hadn't] learned that bullying and breaking promises are no longer cost-free." "Let me put it plainly, he said, "if you strike, you'll get hit." Traffic through the Strait to a near standstill on Thursday, Bloomberg reported. Ship-tracking data showed most vessel movements were confined to the Iran-approved route along the waterway's northern side, while the U.S.-backed Omani shipping corridor saw little activity. Among larger vessels, only a U.S.-sanctioned supertanker departing the Persian Gulf and an Iranian-flagged container ship were visible, although some ships may have been transiting with their tracking systems switched off, the outlet noted. Iran says Khamenei funeral proceeding despite U.S. attacks : Iranian officials Thursday that recent U.S. attacks have not disrupted the funeral procession for the slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, whose body was flown to Mashhad to be buried after week-long processions in Tehran, Qom, and the Iraqi cities of Karbala and Najaf, Al Jazeera reported. Officials said an overnight strike that knocked out the railway linking Tehran to Mashhad had not altered plans, and attributed an eight-hour postponement of the burial, originally set for 6 a.m. local time near the shrine of Imam Reza, to heavy crowds in Iraq rather than the attacks. In a issued on Thursday, Iran's Foreign Ministry accused the U.S. of targeting the railway route to Mashhad in an attempt to overshadow the funeral ceremonies of Khamenei, adding the attack reflected its "inability to comprehend the glory of Iranian patriotism" after the Iranian public's "magnificent and unparalleled" turnout at the funeral, IRNA reported. Lebanon Israeli forces demolish homes in Hadatha, bomb Houla in south Lebanon: Israeli forces a demolition operation targeting several houses in the town of Hadatha in the Bint Jbeil district, the National News Agency (NNA) reported Thursday, despite a U.S.-backed "ceasefire" signed with Lebanon. Israeli forces also bombed the town of Houla in the Marjayoun district, according to NNA. The Israeli army also carried out a series of demolitions overnight and at dawn in the towns of Khiam and Taybeh in Marjayoun. Trump says Israel will withdraw from southern Lebanon; Israel 's defense minister says it won't: U.S. President Donald Trump reporters on Wednesday that he thought Israel would withdraw from southern Lebanon. "I think they want to," he said to reporters, despite recent statements from Netanyahu to the contrary, and citing the recent "framework" deal as the reason for the withdrawal. "Yeah, they'll leave. And I think it's going to work out very well," Trump said. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz rejected these claims on Thursday, saying Israel would stay in Lebanon as long as it deemed necessary, and that it "did not ask permission to enter Lebanon" and "does not need permission to stay in Lebanon." Hezbollah: Lebanon-Israel framework "serves Israel entirely": Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem Wednesday the Lebanon-Israel framework agreement "serves Israel entirely" and called for it to be scrapped, arguing it was unconstitutional, NNA reported. Speaking during a public gathering, Qassem said Israel had committed "hundreds" of ceasefire violations and urged Lebanese authorities to pursue only indirect negotiations. He also said there could be "no solution except Israeli withdrawal" in exchange for the deployment of the Lebanese army south of the Litani River, alongside an end to Israeli attacks, the release of detainees, reconstruction, and the return of displaced residents. He reaffirmed Hezbollah's support for the U.S.-Iran MOU, saying the group would remain committed to resistance. Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed, one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks, and 17 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,118 killed, with 173,615 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,092 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,507, while 799 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli attacks on Gaza continue on Thursday: An Israeli drone strike two Palestinians and wounded several others west of Khan Younis, southern Gaza on Thursday, WAFA reported. Another Palestinian was also killed in a drone strike on a vehicle west of Gaza City. Israeli attacks kill at least eight Palestinians on Wednesday: Israeli attacks across Gaza on Wednesday killed at least eight Palestinians, including multiple children, including an employee of the World Central Kitchen. Israeli forces a driver working for a World Central Kitchen partner logistics company, the charity announced on Wednesday, while he was transporting aid from the Kerem Shalom crossing to a WCK warehouse in Gaza. An Israeli airstrike on Gaza City's Sheikh Radwan neighborhood killed two, while a strike on a vehicle west of Gaza City on Wednesday evening one Palestinian and wounded several others, WAFA reported. Israeli court rejects imprisoned physician 's plea: The** Israeli government on Wednesday to a High Court petition over the detention of Gaza physician Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, saying he has been examined several times since being transferred to the underground Rakefet detention facility, following reports of severe abuse by Israeli forces. The government also asked the court to dismiss, without a hearing, PHRI's petition seeking the release of 14 Gaza doctors, including Dr. Abu Safiya, held without charge. Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI) argued that the state failed to explain why the examinations were necessary, what they found, or to respond to allegations from his lawyer that he suffered severe injuries and repeated loss of consciousness. The group said the decision raises additional questions about Dr. Safiya's well-being. Also on Wednesday, two more U.S. members of Congress called for Dr. Abu Safiya's release. Sen. Bernie Sanders Israel of "kidnapping" Dr. Safiya because he refused to abandon one of Gaza's last hospitals, "even after Israel killed his own son in a drone strike," and unequivocally demanded his "immediate" release. Florida Democrat Valerie Foushee joined Sanders--and Sen. Chris Van Hollen and Democratic congressional nominee Darializa Avila Chevalier before her--in calling for Abu Safiya's release, saying she is "deeply disturbed" by his detention and reports of his abuse in prison. Hamas delegation returns to Cairo for negotiations: A Hamas delegation led by the group's Gaza head, Dr. Khalil al-Hayya, in Cairo on Wednesday to continue ceasefire negotiations with Egyptian and other mediators, according to a statement from senior official Taher Al-Nunu. Al-Nunu said that talks aim to "secure a lasting ceasefire," advance the agreement to its second phase while completing the implementation of its first phase, increase humanitarian aid into Gaza, and accelerate the transfer of governance responsibilities to the National Committee for Administration of Gaza, operating under Trump's "Board of Peace," following the dissolution of the Strip's administration earlier this week. Abbas sets Nov. 28 as date for Palestinian legislative elections: Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas a decree on Thursday setting Saturday, November 28, 2026, as the date for legislative elections, calling on Palestinians in East Jerusalem, the occupied West Bank and the Gaza Strip to participate, according to WAFA. Abbas, who has remained in office since 2005 after repeatedly postponing elections, announced what would be the first parliamentary vote since 2006, when Hamas defeated his Fatah movement. In June, he amended the election law, requiring candidates to endorse the Palestine Liberation Organization as the sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people. Hamas rejected the changes, saying they entrenched political monopoly and lacked national consensus. Israel 's "Crimson Thread" barrier cuts off Palestinian farms in Jordan Valley: Israeli forces are constructing a 22-kilometer separation wall and military road through the Al-Forat farm near Tubas in the northern West Bank, part of a planned 500-kilometer "Crimson Thread" barrier that would seal off the Jordan Valley from the rest of Palestine, Drop Site reports. Farmer Muad Abdelreziq told Drop Site that Israel had cut water access to 400 dunams of farmland for five days and destroyed irrigation pipelines, and a January petition by Tubas residents estimating $200 million in annual economic damage led to a court injunction that Israel's military successfully rescinded days after the U.S. and Israel launched their war on Iran on March 3. "I cannot irrigate the herbs, I cannot irrigate the melons," one farmer said about the changes. "I cannot replace the water lines. All these families will have nothing. We will have to stop." Read the latest from Drop Site 's Maysa Mustafa , and watch Mustafa's video dispatch . U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Graham Platner drops out of Maine Senate race: Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner from the race on Wednesday after a week in which he faced multiple allegations of sexual misconduct, including a rape allegation. In a video posted to X, he called the accusations "all false" and told supporters that he was ending his campaign because the "political reality" was that party leaders and major donors "are going to take everything away from us," making it impossible to continue. Maine Democrats now have until July 27 to choose a replacement for the November race against incumbent Republican Sen. Susan Collins. In his video statement, Platner urged party leaders to make the selection through an "open, transparent and democratic" process that reflects "the will and the values of the people of Maine," not decisions made "in back rooms." The Maine Democratic State Committee voted Wednesday to select a replacement nominee for Graham Platner in the U.S. Senate race through a 600-person nominating convention rather than a statewide caucus, with 500 delegates apportioned by county and the remaining 100 drawn from state committee members. The decision, reported by David Dayen at The American Prospect, reverses earlier sourcing that had pointed toward a caucus and threatens to alienate Platner's supporters, who had pushed for an open process. Read TAP's full report on the nominating process . Also on Wednesday, Spencer Toth , who helped design Platner's grassroots campaign strategy and later became the organizing director for the state's Democratic Party, his immediate resignation, alleging that the Party was excluding grassroots organizers from the selection of the next nominee and saying he could no longer serve it when its decisions were not "consistent with [his] values." His resignation cited a Tuesday statement from the Party that said that Platner's apparatus would "have no role in determining our next nominee for U.S. Senate, nor in determining what this process would look like." Joint Chiefs ' top legal counsel to step down early amid wave of Pentagon exits: Brig. Gen. Eric Widmar , senior legal counsel to Joint Chiefs of Staff Chair Gen. Dan Caine , is nearly a year ahead of schedule, telling ProPublica he is leaving for personal reasons after two years living apart from his wife. Widmar becomes the latest in a string of top military officials to depart the Pentagon since the start of the second Trump administration, following Gen. Chris Donahue 's exit last week, Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George 's ouster in April, and Adm. Alvin Holsey 's removal from Southern Command late last year, all reportedly pushed by War Secretary Pete Hegseth. Johnson weighs introducing bill to end birthright citizenship: Speaker of the House Mike Johnson is bringing legislation to the floor that would bar pregnant women from entering the United States to secure citizenship for their children, according to a report from Politico. The largely symbolic measure, unlikely to survive a Senate filibuster, would give Johnson a way to respond to hard-line Republicans pressing for action after the Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's effort to curtail birthright citizenship. Former Wisconsin judge fined $5,000, avoids prison for helping immigrant evade ICE arrest : Former Milwaukee County JudgeHannah Dugan was Wednesday to a $5,000 fine rather than prison time by U.S. District JudgeLynn Adelman , after being convicted in December of felony obstruction for leading Mexican defendant Eduardo Flores-Ruiz through a private jury door in April 2025 as ICE agents sought to arrest him at her Milwaukee County courthouse. Agents ultimately caught and arrested Flores-Ruiz outside after a foot chase, and he was deported in November. Other International News U.S. to remove Syria from list of "state sponsors of terror": The U.S. on Wednesday that it would delist Syria as a "state sponsor of terror," with Secretary of State Marco Rubio calling the move a "historic step" which would "give the Syrian people a chance at greatness." Rubio added that the decision was made because Syria had made "formal assurances" to the U.S. that it would "not support acts of international terrorism in the future." The announcement came as Trump met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Ankara on Wednesday. Trump praised al-Sharaa for the "unbelievable job" he had done in Syria. "What a job he's doing," he added. The designation has significantly impacted the country's economy since it was announced in 1979. It has limited investment within Syria by preventing U.S.-affiliated companies from doing business in the country and by preventing Syrian companies from banking with U.S.-based financial institutions. The U.S. had lifted other sanctions on the country in May, but this delisting is viewed by many as the most significant step the U.S. has taken to benefit al-Sharaa's government. DRC reports 600 Ebola deaths: At least 600 people have from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, according to data released by the country's government on Wednesday. As the outbreak has grown more severe, many healthcare workers in the Ituri province, one of the hardest-hit, have gone on an unofficial strike because they have not been paid, according to the Associated Press. Some workers report not having been paid wages or bonuses since the outbreak was declared on May 15. Clinical trials for treatment of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus--the dominant strain in this latest outbreak--have also begun this week, according to Al Jazeera. U.S. migrants arrive in Eswatini: Eleven more migrants in Eswatini on Wednesday as part of the Trump administration's "third-country" deportation policy. Wednesday's arrivals bring the total number of deportees to 29, following the country's receipt of $5.1 million from Washington. Only two of these people have been released and repatriated. The "third-country" deportation policy has been challenged as illegal, with lawyers for deportees noting that their clients are being detained after having served time for crimes in the United States. Sudanese Army takes control of Kurmuk: The Sudanese Army the border town of Kurmuk in the Blue Nile region on Wednesday, Sudan Tribune reported, after battles between its forces and those of the Rapid Support Forces and its allied Sudan People's Liberation Movement (SPLM-N). The Sudanese Army has set its sights on Kurmuk for several weeks, launching several operations to secure the surrounding area. The town has frequently changed hands during Sudan's civil war, which began in 2023. Kurmuk is near Sudan's border with Ethiopia, which the Sudanese government has accused of supporting the RSF by allowing its drones to launch from Ethiopia's Bahir Dar airport. Ethiopia's government has rejected these allegations. Separately, a UN probe found on Wednesday that the RSF's actions in its 2025 siege of El-Fasher, which included mass killings, abductions of women and girls, mass gang rapes and forced starvation, amount to genocide. The decision comes after survivors testified to UN human rights officials about being raped in the same room where bodies of recently killed civilians, some of whom were their family members, were still lying on the ground. UN officials recently warned about similar conditions in the city of El-Obeid, a city which has been under assault by the RSF's drones, calling the "signs" of human rights abuses "clear and unmistakable." Brazilian police search former president 's home for weapons: Brazil's federal police the home of former President Jair Bolsonaro for weapons on Wednesday, according to a court ruling reported on by Reuters. Bolsonaro's lawyers insist that nothing was found. Last month, a gun registered to Bolsonaro was seized from one of his security guards at a police checkpoint, even though he was required by a court order to surrender all of his weapons. Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27-year prison term under house arrest after attempting a coup when he lost the 2022 election to current president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Bolsonaro's son, Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro, is Lula's principal right-wing opponent in this year's presidential elections. Trump says he will allow Ukraine to make Patriot interceptors: At a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Ankara Wednesday, President Donald Trump that he would give Ukraine "a license" to make Patriot missile interceptors, calling the move "pretty cool" and "defensive" and saying it would prevent the Ukrainians from "complaining" about insufficient supply. Trump gave no specifics about the license, answering a question about a timeline with only the qualification that "some" could be sent immediately, and that Ukraine would "quickly" be able to produce interceptors of its own. He also hinted that the U.S. would be willing to use its "great power" over the companies that produce the interceptors to secure them for Ukraine. Lockheed Martin is the primary manufacturer of this technology Trump struck a noticeably warm tone with Zelenskyy, with whom he has clashed in the past. He also said he intended to speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin later in the day, though he provided no further details. Russia bans diesel exports: Russia on Wednesday that it would ban the export of its diesel products until the end of July in an attempt to protect its energy markets from the effects of the war in Ukraine, and following several Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. The move, which will significantly tighten the global supply of and demand for refined petroleum products, is expected to have a particular effect on Europe's diesel markets, pushing up costs immediately for farmers and truckers, and eventually for consumers. Ukrainian drones hit Russian tankers: Ukrainian drones hit a dozen Russian tankers in the Sea of Azov overnight, Ukraine's military in a statement, as Kyiv ramps up a campaign aimed at hitting energy infrastructure and disrupting fuel supplies to Russian forces while isolating Moscow-occupied Crimea. Ireland moves to ban imports from Israeli settlements: Ireland's Dail the Occupied Territories Bill on Tuesday without a vote, setting Ireland up to become the first European Union country to legislate a ban on imports from Israeli settlements, according to Irish broadcaster RTÉ. The bill heads to the Seanad next week and is expected to be law before mid-July, making settlement imports an offense under Ireland's Customs Act, the Irish Times reports. The government's version of the bill bans only goods, however, while exempting services, which make up about 70 percent of Ireland's trade with Israel, said a foreign affairs spokesperson for Ireland's Labour Party. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has cited legal risk and potential damage to U.S. multinationals in Ireland if the bill is passed, and the Irish Times reported that Ireland's embassy in Washington has also been warned of "consequences" by its American host. Flooding from Tropical Storm Maysak kills 39 in southern China : Flooding from Tropical Storm Maysak has 39 people in China's southern Guangxi region, including 26 after a dam breach inundated parts of Nanning, officials said Thursday. About 130,000 people have been evacuated, with more than 8,000 rescuers and 5,700 boats deployed after days of heavy rainfall brought up to 90 cm of rain in the hardest-hit areas. Authorities said floodwaters are receding, but more rain is expected, while work continues to clear debris, disinfect towns, repair roads and restore power. Calls to lift Venezuela sanctions grow amid post-earthquake recovery efforts: Venezuelan Acting President Delcy Rodriguez to the U.K. to release 30 tons of gold held by the Bank of England, arguing these resources are vital for reconstruction. Separaely, a coalition of over 100 prominent economists, including Jeffrey Sachs and Isabella Weber, the U.S. to lift all broad economic sanctions, saying the "indiscriminate" measures severely obstruct the humanitarian response and essential post-disaster recovery efforts. subject: As a little girl growing up in Brownsville…
body:
The American Dream has slipped under Abbott’s leadership.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
The American Dream.
When I was a little girl growing up in Brownsville, that phrase used to actually mean something, Peter. It meant if you worked hard, you could do more than just survive — you and your family could thrive.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260709_1_american.py79NP&refcode=em20260709-1527&amount=5&t=1&akid=1527%2E299639%2EgvOiAl)
The American Dream was a promise that if you worked a full-time job, you could afford to own a home. Afford to pay your bills. Afford to raise a family, and maybe even take a vacation now and then. And, yes, that you could afford to retire with dignity.
But under Greg Abbott’s leadership, that dream has slipped away.
Thanks to the Greg Abbott Corruption Tax, we’re stuck paying more and getting less. Because of Abbott’s no-bid contracts, his school voucher scam, and his giveaways to corporate billionaires and ultra-wealthy friends, WE are stuck paying the price.
And let me be crystal clear: Texans are not asking for handouts. We are asking for what we already paid for.
**This November, we have an opportunity to win a better Texas and restore the American Dream.**
[****](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260709_1_american.py79NP&refcode=em20260709-1527&amount=5&t=2&akid=1527%2E299639%2EgvOiAl)
One that rewards hard work and puts the American Dream back within our grasp. But we have to vote for it. We have to work for it. And that means doing all we can to build a campaign capable of taking on Greg Abbott and the billionaires.

Hi there,

I know you hear a lot from my campaign team and me about fundraising,
Republican spending, polling, and a whole bunch of other things, but today
I wanted to send you a different kind of email.

I’ve spent the past week travelling all across Michigan meeting voters,
listening to families, and talking to Michiganders about what’s at stake
in this election. Here’s a look at what I’ve been up to:

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/8179?t=1001&akid=1714%2E181023%2EUB-ksa ]Talking to folks in Bay City

Talking to folks in Bay City. We had a room packed with Michiganders ready
to win in November.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/8179?t=1002&akid=1714%2E181023%2EUB-ksa ]Politics & Pints in Kalamazoo

I couldn’t have asked for a better ending to a busy day on the campaign
trail than with the hardworking folks who came out for Politics & Pints in
Kalamazoo.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/8179?t=1003&akid=1714%2E181023%2EUB-ksa ]Touring the Roosevelt Community Garden in Grand Rapids

Touring the Roosevelt Community Garden in Grand Rapids. This garden brings
neighbors together and creates a space where people can thrive.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/8179?t=1004&akid=1714%2E181023%2EUB-ksa ]Meeting with community members in South Haven

Meeting with community members in South Haven. We talked about the issues
top of mind ahead of November — and it came down to housing and energy
costs.

Every stop on this tour reminds me that Michiganders are ready for
leadership focused on what matters most — lowering costs, raising wages,
standing up for Michiganders, and creating opportunity in every corner of
our state.

I’m that leader, but my leading Republican opponent already has Trump’s
endorsement and $5 million from the DeVos family. That sort of money can
flood the airwaves and define this race before voters have a chance to
hear our message.

To combat the GOP’s millions and get in front of as many voters as
possible, we need to make sure we have the resources to keep meeting folks
where they are, from community gardens to their local Irish pubs.

to help us keep building our campaign and reach as many voters as

subject: A not-very-friendly reminder
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Warren for Senate: https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/370?source=em-header&t=1001&akid=2958%2E4032634%2ELsV9uj

A not-very-friendly reminder:

Donald Trump is refusing to sign legislation to build more housing and
make housing more affordable.

Democrats and Republicans overwhelmingly passed a housing affordability
bill in both the House and the Senate (when was the last time you heard
that?).

Why?

He said he won’t sign unless Congress passes the SAVE Act first — the
restrictive voter ID law that would make it harder for millions of
citizens to vote.

Why?

Because he knows his agenda is unpopular and Republicans can’t win based
on what he’s doing, so he wants to rig the election by picking his own
voters.

That’s what this is all about.

Again, not an ordinary voter ID bill. Trump and the Republicans in
Congress will defend it by saying things like, "You should have to show ID
to vote just like you do to buy a beer."

Don’t let them fool you.

This is a way to keep American citizens from voting. I'll give you an
example:

If this bill passes, then in 45 of 50 states, your driver's license won’t
count as valid ID.

Let’s say you’re a married woman who lives in Massachusetts. And let’s say
that when you got married, you took your husband’s name.

Well, when you go to the polls to vote, you can't register by showing them
your updated driver’s license. Why? Because Massachusetts is one of the 45
states where a driver’s license doesn’t prove citizenship.

So you bring along your birth certificate? Now can you vote?

Nope. Your birth certificate is still under your maiden name.

Yes, you can use a passport, if you have one. But remember that fewer than
half of all Americans have a passport and it costs $165 to get one — and
takes a month or two, if everything is working on time.

No passport and no birth certificate that matches your driver’s license?
Well, Trump and the Republicans say you’re out of luck.

Here’s another deeply disturbing thing about this bill: it would require
states to hand over sensitive information about voters to Trump’s
Department of Homeland Security, so that some shadowy guys can do whatever
they want with it.

Maybe they take you off the voter rolls. Maybe they use that information
for something else. No one knows what will happen.

Guess who's going to get swept off the voter rolls? People that the
Republicans think are likely to vote Democratic.

So, sweep off Black people, sweep off Brown people, sweep off women, sweep
off students, sweep off people in precincts who voted Democratic last
time, sweep off people that you think might vote Democratic in the
upcoming election.

This Trump bill is Jim Crow 2.0.

And noncitizen voting is extremely rare. Republicans know that.

They’ve seen the data: Voter roll audits in Georgia prior to the 2024
election found only 20 registered noncitizens out of 8.2 million
registered voters, or 0.00024%.

A 2024 Michigan audit found only 16 noncitizen votes out of 5.7 million
votes, or 0.00028%.

So, yep: The President of the United States is blocking critical housing
legislation that would make rent more affordable and help people actually
be able to buy a home in order to rig the rules and pick their own voters.

I’m going to keep up the fight to get this plan passed — and while Trump
and Republicans try to spread conspiracies and lie about the SAVE Act,
it’s important that we send a clear message that the American people say
NO to passing the SAVE Act.

[ https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-noSAVE26/?source=EW_EMZ32H_SAV_ENG_20260709_F&t=1006&akid=2958%2E4032634%2ELsV9uj ]Republicans are pulling every lever they can to wage an assault on our
democracy and cling onto their power. We can’t — and won’t let them. We
need to demonstrate that the American people are outright rejecting the
SAVE Act. Please add your name to say you do not support this legislation.

[ https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-noSAVE26/?source=EW_EMZ32H_SAV_ENG_20260709_F&t=1007&akid=2958%2E4032634%2ELsV9uj ]ADD YOUR NAME

Thanks for being a part of this,

Elizabeth
