It has been one year since Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill” became law, and the results have been anything but beautiful.

Americans are facing higher prices, higher inflation, slower job growth, and an economy that works best for those already on top.

Since the passage of this legislation, 17 million Americans have lost health insurance. More than 4 million Americans, including 800,000 children, have already lost access to basic food assistance. Meanwhile, the wealthiest .1% have received tax cuts worth a nearly quarter-million dollars just last year.

**The so-called Big Beautiful Bill is nothing but welfare for the wealthy and well-connected.**

name: The Maine Democrats
subject: What happens now in Maine:
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems]
This week, we called on our own nominee for the U.S. Senate to withdraw. We hold every candidate who seeks to carry our banner to the highest standard, and we stand with women and survivors. That principle does not bend based on party affiliation.
He has now withdrawn.
The hard decision in this story was not ours. It belonged to the women who came forward, because speaking up is often costly, and we respect them for it.
Our responsibility required judgment and a willingness to act when circumstances demanded it. Circumstances demanded it. We acted.
Now we want to talk to you about what happens next, because it matters enormously.
There is no Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in Maine.
Our party will come together, as our rules provide, to choose the Democrat who will carry our banner against Susan Collins. We will do it carefully and we will do it right. Mainers deserve nothing less.
But here is the hard truth about that gap:
Susan Collins does not pause while we confer. She has been raising money for this race for six years. Her campaign is raising more today, and it will raise more tomorrow. The corporate PACs and wealthy interests her votes protect are not waiting to see who our nominee is. They are adding to a war chest six years in the making, while our side has no candidate, no campaign, and no one answering. Whoever we choose will start this race six years behind.
Every day of this holding period is a day she banks money unanswered.
We refuse to let our next nominee start from zero.
So the Maine Democratic Party is opening the Day One Fund: money raised now, held ready, so that the moment our new nominee is chosen, they inherit a running start instead of an empty account.
Day one, they will need a statewide organizing operation already paid for.
Day one, they will need voter contact already underway in all 16 counties.
Day one, they will need to answer Collins on the air, not spend a month catching up.
That is what this fund does. Not a bailout, not a rainy-day account. A running start, waiting for whoever earns the nomination. Can you help power us with a split contribution between Maine Democrats and Equal Opportnity Now today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE TODAY TO THE DAY ONE FUND! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems]
This Senate race comes at a pivotal moment in the struggle against a government, supported by Senator Collins, that serves the interests of the wealthy and powerful at the expense of ordinary Maine people. That struggle did not end this week. If anything, our responsibility to it grew.
The party will do its job in the days ahead. We are asking you to do yours today, so that our nominee, whoever they are, walks into this fight ready. Will you chip in a split contribution between Maine Dems and Equal Opportunity Now today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems]
CHIP IN BEFORE OUR NOMINEE IS CHOSEN! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems]
Thank you for your support,
The Maine Democrats

body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=41ca076dce&e=a7ab36849c)
| | | | | |
Good afternoon, freedom fighters!
I wanted to take a short break from the campaign trail to send you an update on my whereabouts and important election information. On the campaign trail, I continue meeting voters daily. A voter I just met told me she had just mailed back her ballot and cast a vote for me. She was thrilled to meet me at her doorstep — even in 100‐degree extreme heat. Her encouragement along with countless other supporters keeps me going.
🏡 Housing Affordability: A Crisis We Must Confront 🏘️Affordability and finding solutions aren’t just talking points for me — they’ve been a priority since my time in the House. I sponsored legislation to eliminate the rental tax, and more recently I participated in the American Enterprise Institute’s Housing Abundance Roadshow: Practical Solutions for Local Growth.At this event, we discussed the growing challenge everyday Arizonans face in affording housing and the obstacles of passing and advancing meaningful reforms at the legislature. Even new attorneys being recruited to Arizona with six‐figure incomes can’t afford an entry‐level home. If young working professionals can’t afford rising housing costs in our state, we are beyond a crisis. Arizona’s long‐term economic strength depends on attracting and retaining the best and brightest workforce. Right now, we are failing to provide an adequate supply of different housing options. Other states are moving forward with bipartisan legislative reforms — deregulation, permitting reform, rezoning — showing that solutions exist. For the past two years, I’ve worked on legislation to allow smaller homes on smaller lots and to push back against city bureaucrats who want to dictate aesthetics or require shared amenities that force first‐time homeowners into HOAs. Sadly, taxpayer‐funded lobbyists have blocked many of these reforms. I remain committed to this fight.
🎨 Community Spotlight: Taiwanese Art Exhibit at the Old CapitolLast week, I joined a ribbon‐cutting ceremony for a new Taiwanese art exhibit at [Arizona’s Old Capitol ](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=c71ef5f189&e=a7ab36849c)featuring Taiwan artist Chris Ho and his remarkable American eagle paintings. If you have time, I encourage you to visit.I also offered brief remarks to the Taiwanese Younger Leaders group, who received medals alongside local supporters. Many employees of TSMC live in LD2, and their children attend several DVUSD schools — making this cultural connection especially meaningful for our local community.
🗳️ July 21 Primary Election: Make a Plan to VoteArizona’s primary election is underway. If you are on the Active Early Voting List (AEVL), you should have received your early ballot more than a week ago. Please research the candidates, complete your ballot, and return it as soon as possible.I voted early in person at ASU West last week. If you prefer in‐person early voting, I highly recommend making a plan.Voting by mail: 📬 Mail your ballot back as soon as possible to ensure it is counted.Maricopa County votersFind your nearest polling location: [https://elections.maricopa.gov/voting/where-to-vote.html](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=fbe7b14f9c&e=a7ab36849c)Outside Maricopa County:Verify registration, find your polling place, and track your ballot: [https://my.arizona.vote/PortalList.aspx](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=9fb49089dc&e=a7ab36849c)Voting is one of our most important civic duties. Every election shapes the future of our communities. I encourage you to make your voice heard on or before July 21.🇺🇸 America 250: Reflecting on Our FoundingI wasn’t in Washington, D.C. for the July 4th festivities, but I took time out of my crazy schedule to reflect on our nation’s founding. Last month, I traveled to Philadelphia for a Republican women’s leadership policy summit and visited the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall.Sitting in the room where our Founders debated and drafted one of history’s most important documents was a powerful reminder that America remains a beacon of freedom. Defending and protecting our constitutional rights preserves the freedoms that make Arizona exceptional.Relive America 250 highlights: [https://live.america250.org](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=95b0567669&e=a7ab36849c)
📄 Ballot Analysis for the November ElectionThis week, House and Senate members met to discuss and vote on ballot analysis language for the November election. clean_body: | | | | | | | | | | | Good afternoon, freedom fighters! I wanted to take a short break from the campaign trail to send you an update on my whereabouts and important election information. On the campaign trail, I continue meeting voters daily. A voter I just met told me she had just mailed back her ballot and cast a vote for me. She was thrilled to meet me at her doorstep — even in 100‐degree extreme heat. Her encouragement along with countless other supporters keeps me going. 🏡 Housing Affordability: A Crisis We Must Confront 🏘️Affordability and finding solutions aren’t just talking points for me — they’ve been a priority since my time in the House. I sponsored legislation to eliminate the rental tax, and more recently I participated in the American Enterprise Institute’s Housing Abundance Roadshow: Practical Solutions for Local Growth.At this event, we discussed the growing challenge everyday Arizonans face in affording housing and the obstacles of passing and advancing meaningful reforms at the legislature. Even new attorneys being recruited to Arizona with six‐figure incomes can’t afford an entry‐level home. If young working professionals can’t afford rising housing costs in our state, we are beyond a crisis. Arizona’s long‐term economic strength depends on attracting and retaining the best and brightest workforce. Right now, we are failing to provide an adequate supply of different housing options. Other states are moving forward with bipartisan legislative reforms — deregulation, permitting reform, rezoning — showing that solutions exist. For the past two years, I’ve worked on legislation to allow smaller homes on smaller lots and to push back against city bureaucrats who want to dictate aesthetics or require shared amenities that force first‐time homeowners into HOAs. Sadly, taxpayer‐funded lobbyists have blocked many of these reforms. I remain committed to this fight. 🎨 Community Spotlight: Taiwanese Art Exhibit at the Old CapitolLast week, I joined a ribbon‐cutting ceremony for a new Taiwanese art exhibit at Taiwan artist Chris Ho and his remarkable American eagle paintings. If you have time, I encourage you to visit.I also offered brief remarks to the Taiwanese Younger Leaders group, who received medals alongside local supporters. Many employees of TSMC live in LD2, and their children attend several DVUSD schools — making this cultural connection especially meaningful for our local community. 🗳️ July 21 Primary Election: Make a Plan to VoteArizona’s primary election is underway. If you are on the Active Early Voting List (AEVL), you should have received your early ballot more than a week ago. Please research the candidates, complete your ballot, and return it as soon as possible.I voted early in person at ASU West last week. If you prefer in‐person early voting, I highly recommend making a plan.Voting by mail: 📬 Mail your ballot back as soon as possible to ensure it is counted.Maricopa County votersFind your nearest polling location: Maricopa County:Verify registration, find your polling place, and track your ballot: is one of our most important civic duties. Every election shapes the future of our communities. I encourage you to make your voice heard on or before July 21.🇺🇸 America 250: Reflecting on Our FoundingI wasn’t in Washington, D.C. for the July 4th festivities, but I took time out of my crazy schedule to reflect on our nation’s founding. Last month, I traveled to Philadelphia for a Republican women’s leadership policy summit and visited the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall.Sitting in the room where our Founders debated and drafted one of history’s most important documents was a powerful reminder that America remains a beacon of freedom. Defending and protecting our constitutional rights preserves the freedoms that make Arizona exceptional.Relive America 250 highlights: 📄 Ballot Analysis for the November ElectionThis week, House and Senate members met to discuss and vote on ballot analysis language for the November election. | | Peter,
This year, as we mark 250 years in this great experiment in liberty, I keep asking myself the same question: _**Are we keeping the faith?** _
Let me explain what I mean.
At the very heart of it, _we were born a nation of Christian pilgrims and dissenters. _
The Pilgrims. The Puritans. The Quakers. The Huguenots. The German Pietists. Wave after wave of men and women who crossed an ocean because they refused to let any earthly power stand between them and their biblical faith in the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob – the God revealed in Jesus Christ.
_That is the seed America grew from_ , and every time we’ve forgotten this, we’ve gone astray.
The very first freedom in the Bill of Rights – the one the framers put first, not fifth or tenth, but first – is **the freedom to worship God without interference from government**. That wasn’t random. It was the whole point.
And when people knock our founding fathers as relics of a bygone era who “wouldn’t understand the world today,” I ask you to think about our brothers and sisters in Christ today, _right now_ , in places like Nigeria, Iran, Pakistan, North Korea and many other places.
**There are an estimated 388 million Christian men, women and children being persecuted, oppressed and ruthlessly murdered simply for loving Jesus.**
Here in America, _it’s almost impossible to know what that’s like_ , but we do have the freedom, the platform and the resources to support them, and fight back in a wide range of ways. **The question is, will we?**
I can’t help but feel that this year, on the 250th birthday of the world’s most indispensable Christian nation, that we have a duty to rededicate ourselves to God and to the defense of His people around the world. **And today, I’m asking you to partner with me and an incredible organization in that endeavor.**
**There is no organization in this country more committed to that fight than Save the Persecuted Christians, where I’m proud to serve as a board member.** ** ** Whether it’s the growing awareness of the active genocide against Nigeria’s Christians (and recent U.S. action to help stop it), or the recent and very real victories against the rise of sharia and Islamism here in America, it is due in very large part to the relentless advocacy and education campaigns of Save the Persecuted Christians and the coalition of 200+ organizations they help to guide.
[ **As we commemorate America’s 250th birthday, I humbly but urgently ask that you help to supercharge their efforts with a generous, tax-deductible contribution.** ](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=44c79468774f45a583e6029c7f70f92e&_e=o5mEs9M7xHe3vTPvjzYsirzGtUZy_3nFg35ZugALAMvZ9mgwJabMveNY864UCTuSnuluzO02KcY24yH4pOHYniddlBqpMjF3904kyIDZ8zkF3DSw440yyl48NDvpqTlqzyN5U6-GRr7tvhZUtep5SjC1d0edTIwAkcQox2DOw7uVTaYYvcsmoKeZWZFeCba830RpL_NPrrIQzVMDqioltQYgNJxbTW18h7RcpMiJaNzQdGBos73FJds8oRnRg0-RNlVfnWw_svxtwRtVMtVH0w7UE3KpTBuAaPM19rjVK2Au4_j7qXBjHWLY_OPC34Qg4CYVoBP-1i5jHVhJt9Ty86EmOQMiq93PEgizk5HceiYXb0-3CP8qCc6jD0Rl_VJfSpF869uoFGbGGAtYqjxMKjsKTRNgIF4EN8MrmkBxJnNP7lLXJBDnuzj9mBfh6FJnQ3ojIrSdxWsbwr3ANw2UQX-WztEaaMk4ML4_WI5Ktx5lpVKF0L-mGV7u6Rj-E3kR88FPvTXFVaW_PTMogZ0QVXQgUuHS-mZxgoQyNN2XguYXIzu4TBAQ95Oq0kre02JWn3K4EBZ8_G2nLMyQLSukuBcGH2ZlL1GmSQLCUH5xdSauJ7_vk_72FTnW-fYSMz3lfe18brFnCSbFgogv-P6JKKm1P8qJZVDjhXfkbKfynm2Mw64ZZrFRvKAzYg743df_GSpUJmI6klABY22bKgmBOYMDtEZHQoB0xch5-S97NzdGsQS0_0_9kefAjbITzFHm)

As you contemplate your potential commitment, I ask you to think about this.
**While Christians in America today are the freest Christians in the history of the world, 388 million of our brothers and sisters, in other parts of the world, are being hunted for practicing the same faith that built this country.**
Every generation that ever mattered to the kingdom of God understood that faith without action is sentiment – and sentiment has never freed a single soul.
**Now it's our turn.**
Two hundred and fifty years ago, the founders pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor. _They paid the price._ They handed us the inheritance. The only real question this year is what we do with it.
On July 3, 1776 – one day after the Continental Congress had voted to declare independence – John Adams sat down in Philadelphia and wrote to his wife Abigail.
He told her this new American holiday " _ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance, by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations, from one End of this Continent to the other, from this Time forward forever more._ "
Notice the order. _First solemn devotion to God._ Then the fireworks.
250 years later, we’ve kept the fireworks. But the question is, have we maintained the devotion?
I believe we still can. **This anniversary is bigger than a birthday party. It is a reckoning** – with our history, with our blessings, and with our obligations to the brothers and sisters around the world who are paying the highest possible price for the very faith we still get to practice openly.
They are praying for a Church that does not always remember their names.
On this 250th birthday – of all years – we have the chance to tell them they are not forgotten.
[ **That is what your gift does. That is what Save the Persecuted Christians does. And that is why, I am asking you to give as generously as you possibly can.** ](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=44c79468774f45a583e6029c7f70f92e&_e=o5mEs9M7xHe3vTPvjzYsirzGtUZy_3nFg35ZugALAMvZ9mgwJabMveNY864UCTuSnuluzO02KcY24yH4pOHYniddlBqpMjF3904kyIDZ8zkF3DSw440yyl48NDvpqTlqzyN5U6-GRr7tvhZUtep5SjC1d0edTIwAkcQox2DOw7uVTaYYvcsmoKeZWZFeCba830RpL_NPrrIQzVMDqioltQYgNJxbTW18h7RcpMiJaNzQdGBos73FJds8oRnRg0-RNlVfnWw_svxtwRtVMtVH00oyEDCohSbo2XQvmweviCU3vRo65OcnbonhUOIFw1qeeoeix_UYQIQqou3bo473LLB8o192Q5RszTfH5BFHsdZZZDSjxveYVy8n1_s22TSKaX7yAuRW38y7NUUuwyRVzG3KM08g0Z_RBNy5UXuQA60j7A7PapLyZDPAH_TRBMaHJVacrBx0UE2-d5ohZMF6sR6en0qC6jI04tZeAFBFIxWQWwqeduSOw4AfmSdtF3n6zVb_w4Yp4-78zpWggrb4UCLmsnFBEYYuwszWV5w1xv55r47k8eULXaEpMfNvhKP8ZeZYIe_oUZHDYC2lJKbU9JCnUwkRgJ7IvWocokqBv_vEhcqHCcl3qzKbDcBgGIvYV2eZBLEICJUmN_vlE_qLq142K2_DZGFhQ5EHc1uNYIoUN8VsSm09oefEiiwe8SK9s9CeLANTZC9oNTX0xcom4iUcjVMI2u6ppZYeMmX2WsTzwtW3UYlCocqesBgsMnk3)

We are racking up wins. **We’ve been officially recognized by the DCCC as a Red to Blue race – making us one of their top priorities this November. This comes the day after a brand new poll was released showing us LEADING in this battleground district.** It’s a sign that they know that we have what it takes to beat Mike Lawler and flip NY-17. That’s only possible because of the strength of this grassroots team. So thank you. Please know: I do not take my responsibility to beat Mike Lawler lightly. But we are beginning the general election at a massive fundraising disadvantage, and today’s announcement is going to bring more MAGA money pouring into our race. We’re in for a tough fight. But I’ve never backed down from a tough fight in my life. I joined the Army after 9/11. _You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2628%2E259176%2EiswEY2) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2628%2E259176%2EiswEY2)_

I was inside the Capitol when the mob broke through. I heard the shouting in the hallways. I watched my colleagues scramble for safety. When it was over, when the glass had been swept up and the blood had been scrubbed off the marble floors, I went back to the House floor and voted to certify the 2020 election. And then, a few weeks later, I voted to impeach Donald Trump. I did both of those things because I believed the truth mattered. Because I believed that what happened that day was not a protest, not a tourist visit, not a false flag: it was an attempt to overturn a free and fair election, and the people responsible needed to be held accountable. I'm telling you all of this because I launched something new to fight back against Donald Trump and his attacks on our democracy, and I need you with me. **[_I'm launching Back the Bold because I believe in electing Democrats who aren’t afraid to be bold and fight back against Trump. But, Peter, I have spent every day and every year since watching this country get gaslit.
Watching the people who stormed those halls get pardoned and even _hired_ by Trump. Watching the officials who planned and enabled it get rewarded. Watching a man who incited a mob against his own government run for president again and win.
And I’ve questioned how we fix this broken system, how we fix our democracy, how we fight back against Trump’s blatant abuses of power.
**The best way I can think of fixing this is by electing politicians who refuse to look the other way. Period.**
That's why I launched Back the Bold.
We're supporting candidates who dare to stand up to MAGA extremism and hold politicians in Washington accountable. **Candidates who will say what needs to be said, do what needs to be done, and put country before politics.**

body:

| | | | | |
Every paycheck in New Mexico gets a bite taken out of it for state income tax. This week, one of the most powerful people in Santa Fe [said out loud what almost no one will](https://us.list-manage.com/PKIyy9_VguA?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e): the state doesn't need a dime of it. And he's not a Republican.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/MDY0yygWXO0?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | **🏛️ NEW MEXICO DOESN'T NEED YOUR INCOME TAX — AND SANTA FE KNOWS IT**

Sen. George Muñoz runs the Senate Finance Committee. That's what makes his op-ed impossible to wave off. He opens with the food-bank numbers, then points to one investment figure that quietly makes the whole case for wiping the tax out. Mark says every Republican would vote for it tomorrow.

The real question is what happens when Muñoz's own side reads it.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/10gYUG7yZBZ?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)

You know the type - the student who doesn't back down from a challenge, who pushes through when it gets hard, who brings out the best in everyone around them. The 2026 Patriot Games are calling their name. As part of Freedom 250, the official celebration of our Nation's 250th birthday, this is their chance to show the country what they're made of.
High school students ages 14-17 will compete in challenges built to test strength, speed, agility, teamwork, resilience, and leadership - with a **$250,000 scholarship prize pool** and a nationally televised, prime-time special with ESPN on ABC coverage on August 13th.
**Share this with that student and tell them to Apply TODAY!** This is their moment.
[Apply Now! Don't let this opportunity pass by - share it with every outstanding student you know and encourage them to Apply TODAY!](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
